claims.statement: ARDoCo's pipeline is a three-level composite: AbstractExecutionStage extends Pipeline and holds PipelineAgents, PipelineAgent extends Pipeline and holds Informants, and Pipeline.process() executes its added steps strictly sequentially — a stage runs its agents one after another and each agent runs its informants one after another (depth-first).

Every pipeline component shares the AbstractPipelineStep lifecycle: run() calls before(), then process(), then after(); Pipeline sets a finished flag in after() (exposed via hasFinished()) and logs the wall-clock duration of each child step.

Pipeline components communicate only through the shared DataRepository blackboard: it stores PipelineStepData in a sorted map keyed by String id, getData(id, class) returns an Optional that is empty for unknown ids or failed casts, addData overwrites with a logged warning, and every AbstractPipelineStep holds the same repository instance instead of references to other steps.

Stages gate agents and agents gate informants at run time: AbstractExecutionStage declares @Configurable @ChildClassConfigurable List<String> enabledAgents (defaulting to all constructor-provided agent ids) and adds only matching agents in preparePipelineSteps(); PipelineAgent does the same for enabledInformants in initialize().

Stages and agents initialize their state during preparation, not construction: AbstractExecutionStage.preparePipelineSteps() (final) invokes the abstract initializeState() before adding agents — e.g. TextExtraction creates and stores its TextStateImpl if absent — while PipelineAgent.initialize() invokes a default no-op initializeState() before adding informants.

AbstractConfigurable applies configuration by reflection over the class hierarchy: fields annotated @Configurable are matched by key — default '<SimpleClassName>::<fieldName>', overridable via @Configurable(key=...), and with @ChildClassConfigurable the concrete subclass name replaces the declaring class name (combining both on a field throws) — @NoConfiguration skips a class level; supported value types are Integer, Double, Boolean, enums by constant name, and comma-separated List<String>, everything else is rejected.

ConfigurationHelper.loadAdditionalConfigs(File) parses UTF-8 files with one 'KEY::attribute=VALUE' line per entry (blank lines skipped, malformed lines logged, a non-existing file throws), and getDefaultConfigurationOptions() reflects over all concrete non-test AbstractConfigurable subclasses under edu.kit.kastel.mcse.ardoco to record every @Configurable field's default value as a string.

Configuration flows down the same composite that executes steps: each Pipeline re-applies its last applied configuration to child steps in preparePipelineSteps(), stages additionally apply it to all agents, agents to all informants, and stage/agent static factories (e.g. TextExtraction.get(additionalConfigs, dataRepository)) construct the component and then call applyConfiguration.

The ArchUnit rule configurableFieldsOnlyInConfigurableClasses in BasicArchitectureTest enforces that @Configurable fields may only be declared in classes assignable to AbstractConfigurable, so reflection-based configuration cannot escape the framework.

Ardoco is the pipeline entry point: it extends Pipeline with id "ARDoCo", creates its own DataRepository, seeds it with ProjectPipelineDataImpl carrying the project name, and runAndSave(outputDir) returns null when no steps were added, otherwise runs the pipeline, wraps the repository in an ArdocoResult, and saves outputs before returning the result.

runAndSave writes three output kinds into the output directory via FilePrinter: traceLinks_<project>.txt (human-readable trace links), inconsistencyDetection_<project>.txt, and per-type CSVs (sadSamTlr_, samCodeTlr_, sadCodeTlr_ prefixed with the project name) that are only written when that link type is non-empty.

ArdocoRunner owns an isSetUp flag and a nullable output directory: final run() returns an ArdocoResult only when isSetUp() is true AND an output directory was set, otherwise it logs an error and returns null; final runWithoutSaving() requires only isSetUp(), runs the pipeline, and returns the raw DataRepository without writing files; concrete runners (e.g. Arcotl, InconsistencyDetection) add steps in setUp(...), call the protected setOutputDirectory(...), then flip isSetUp = true.

AnonymousRunner performs setup eagerly in its constructor: setUp() fetches the Ardoco data repository, calls the abstract initializePipelineSteps(dataRepository) (which typically loads input data and may throw IOException), adds every returned AbstractPipelineStep to Ardoco, and returns true — an IOException sets isSetUp to false.

ArdocoResult is the public typed read API over the DataRepository: a record exposing project name, Text, metamodels, models, trace links (getArchitectureTraceLinks, getSamCodeTraceLinks, getSadCodeTraceLinks) and inconsistencies; per-metamodel state accessors log a warning and return null when the corresponding state container is missing (derived accessors then yield empty collections), whereas getPreprocessingData()/getText() throw when preprocessing never ran.

The SAM intermediate model is metamodel-independent: sealed ArchitectureItem permits ArchitectureComponent, ArchitectureInterface, and ArchitectureMethod; components hold subcomponents plus provided/required interfaces and a type, interfaces hold ArchitectureMethod signatures; ArchitectureModelWithComponentsAndInterfaces accepts only component/interface roots and returns them as trace-link endpoints. PCM/UML/component-listing extractors (e.g. PcmExtractor) produce it.

ArchitectureModel.createArchitectureModelDto() flattens the component/interface/method tree into an id-keyed ArchitectureModelDto: ArchitectureItemRepository holds the sorted map of id → item DTO plus the root content id list; the sealed ArchitectureItemDto permits ComponentDto, InterfaceDto, MethodDto (JSON-discriminated by a 'type' property); each DTO stores children only as id sets (subcomponentsIds, providedInterfacesIds, requiredInterfacesIds, methodSignaturesIds); ArchitectureMethod has a (name, id) constructor so deserialized methods keep their identifier.

ArchitectureExtractor.writeOutArchitectureModel(model, file) serializes an ArchitectureModel to the conventional .aam file name (architectureModel.aam) via JsonHandling.createObjectMapper() and createArchitectureModelDto(); no main-source code path reads an ArchitectureModelDto back into an ArchitectureModel, so the .aam output is currently a write-only cache/export artifact.

The code model is a repository-backed tree: sealed CodeItem permits CodeModule (CodeAssembly, CodeCompilationUnit, CodePackage), ComputationalObject (ControlElement), and Datatype (ClassUnit, InterfaceUnit); every item registers itself in an id-keyed CodeItemRepository, relationships and content are stored as id lists resolved via getCodeItemsByIds, and the model is rooted by CodeModelWithCompilationUnits or CodeModelWithCompilationUnitsAndPackages selected by Metamodel.CODE_WITH_COMPILATION_UNITS[_AND_PACKAGES].

Datatype and ControlElement carry 1-indexed, inclusive startLine/endLine source ranges serialized via @JsonProperty and defaulting to -1 when unknown; extractors populate them (the JDT JavaModel derives them from CompilationUnit.getLineNumber of the declaration start and of start+length, and passes them into the ClassUnit/InterfaceUnit/ControlElement constructors).

Content ownership in the code model lives on the sealed Datatype base, which stores the content id list and provides getContent(), getContentIds() (via @JsonGetter("content")), and getAllDataTypes(), plus compilationUnitId/parentDatatypeId and extended/implemented/datatype-reference id lists; ClassUnit and InterfaceUnit only add type-specific constructors including (content, startLine, endLine) variants.

Model ids survive serialization: Model has a protected Model(String id) constructor where a null id falls back to IdentifierProvider.createId(), CodeModel.CodeModelDto carries the model id alongside the CodeItemRepository and content ids, and CodeModelWithCompilationUnits(dto)/CodeModelWithCompilationUnitsAndPackages(dto) rebuild a model that retains its original id.

Identity in the code model follows the relationship fields: equals/hashCode of Datatype include compilationUnitId, parentDatatypeId, startLine, endLine, extended/implemented/datatype-reference ids, and content; ControlElement adds startLine/endLine and calleeNames; CodeCompilationUnit adds pathElements, extension, language, and importedModuleNames — so deserialized instances stay identity-stable.

The code model records module imports and function callees: CodeCompilationUnit and CodeAssembly expose getImportedModuleNames() as @JsonProperty-serialized List<String> fields defaulting to empty, ControlElement exposes getCalleeNames() the same way, and CodeCompilationUnit.fromRelativePath(...) derives name, pathElements, and extension from a forward-slash relative path while accepting the import list (used by the Python3 mapper, whereas the Java mappers assemble constructor arguments directly).

Only Java and Shell code extraction is wired in pipelines: AllLanguagesExtractor — the code extractor instantiated by the only main-source factory, CodeConfiguration.extractors() in DIRECTORY mode — maps ProgrammingLanguage.JAVA to the Eclipse-JDT JavaExtractor and ProgrammingLanguage.SHELL to ShellExtractor; the ANTLR4 Java, C++, and Python3 extractors/mappers under generators/antlr exist and populate the same fields, but no main-source wiring references them (they are exercised by tests only).

The wired JDT-based JavaModel populates the cross-element code-model fields: extractImportedModuleNames reads each import declaration's fully-qualified name into the CodeCompilationUnit's importedModuleNames, and an ASTVisitor over each method declaration collects MethodInvocation identifiers and ClassInstanceCreation type names as the ControlElement's calleeNames.

Code models round-trip end-to-end: CodeExtractor.writeOutCodeModel serializes createCodeModelDto() to codeModel.acm next to the code directory, and readInCodeModel(file, metamodel) deserializes the CodeModelDto and reconstructs the matching CodeModel subclass (triggering CodeItemRepository.init() to re-register items).

All extracted models are stored in a single ModelStates PipelineStepData (ID "ModelStatesData") keyed by Metamodel, added by ModelProviderInformant after extraction (also for models read from an .acm file); ArdocoResult and stage states resolve models and per-metamodel state through these keys.

The Text intermediate representation preserves the NLP annotations downstream stages rely on: Text exposes sentences and words, Sentence exposes phrases, and Word exposes POS tag, lemma, and incoming/outgoing dependency words by DependencyTag; PreprocessingData (ID "PreprocessingData") carries the preprocessed Text in the repository, and NlpInformant is the abstract Informant that supplies annotated texts.

All model elements descend from the sealed Entity (id + name, Serializable, IdentifierProvider-generated ids): Entity permits TextEntity and ModelEntity, and ModelEntity permits ArchitectureEntity and CodeEntity; ModelEntity adds getType()/getTypeParts() used for name/type-based matching in trace linking.

Each pipeline stage communicates through well-known state identifiers in the repository: TextState, ConnectionStates, RecommendationStates, InconsistencyStates, NerConnectionStates, and CodeTraceabilityState declare String ID constants; the model-dependent stages use per-Metamodel container states (ConnectionStates/RecommendationStates/InconsistencyStates) that resolve the state for a metamodel, and ArdocoResult reads them through the same IDs.
